20.theme: Halloween night party in an old British bungalow
20.title: ভ্যান্স কুঠির অভিশাপ 🎃 | পর্ব ১
20.summary: Soumya, Rini, Debu, and Mitali travel to Vance Kuthi—an abandoned 1860s indigo planter's estate in Nadia—for an ironic Victorian Halloween party on a Kartik Saturday. Caretaker Haru Mondal warns them that the river tide will flood the causeway by eight o'clock, cutting them off until morning, and strictly forbids touching the old hearth. Ignoring the warnings, the group settles in, but Rini's sound recorder detects mechanical grain-scale clangs and breathing beneath the floor. Debu opens loose floorboards near the fireplace, uncovering 160-year-old unhusked rice and a sealed basement vault. As Soumya mockingly acts out a colonial auction, the liquid in their glasses turns into stinking indigo dye, and a terrifying draft snuffs out their light in the cellar. Attempting to flee, they discover the causeway is underwater and their car engine is stuffed with river mud. Locked inside, they hear 44 invisible bare feet pacing outside, and Debu confesses that planter Archibald Vance starved 44 villagers in that cell before being trapped there himself. As the episode ends, Vance's spectral shadow emerges from the open floor holding an iron ledger.
20.part2_plan: Part 2 begins immediately as Vance's shadow demands their signatures on the century-old seed ledger to release the trapped souls. The group must decide whether to attempt a desperate escape through the surging river or face the subterranean granary vault to destroy the original debt contracts. Rini discovers her recorded sound frequencies can temporarily repel the phantom when played at maximum resonance. Debu's failing health forces Mitali to take a perilous lead in finding the original iron bolt that locked the vault. Ultimately, the ancestral sky-lamps across the river must be re-lit to break Archibald Vance's legal curse and grant peace to the forty-four ryots.

10.theme: a new flat in an old building
10.title: কার্তিকের কুয়াশায় সেলাই করা দেয়াল 🕯️
10.summary: Subimal Dutta rents an abnormally cheap first-floor flat in an old Bagbazar mansion during Kartik, noticing a strange cold draft and sour smell from the north wall. Landlord Aloknath forces him to touch the hemp rope for the rooftop sky lamp ritual. Subimal discovers magnetic anomalies, hollow echoes, and a hidden chamber behind his bedroom wall, warned by sweeper Manju against fire and smoke. Measuring the room reveals five missing feet, and twilight reveals sunken eyes watching him from the terracotta flue. Confronting Aloknath yields only missing blueprints and lime-covered fingers. Unlocking the service alcove, Subimal finds tallow-smeared grain weights, and his desk ink congeals into grain units. He unearths a 1943 ledger containing accountant Haripada Bose's final entry and mummified thumb. Discovering Aloknath's terror-stricken confession about his grandfather walling Haripada alive for grain hoarding, the rooftop sky lamp's hemp rope snaps from acid corrosion. The north wall bursts open, spilling rotting black seed rice and releasing the mummified skeleton of Haripada Bose, chained with Saha family crest padlocks, who traps Aloknath against the brick wall.
10.part2_plan: The second part begins immediately with Subimal trapped in the room as the north wall collapses completely, swallowing Aloknath into the grain vault. Subimal must navigate the dark mansion while the ghost of Haripada Bose locks all exit doors and demands the final grain balance sheet. As the Bagbazar neighborhood sleeps through Amavasya, Subimal uncovers the hidden second ledger buried beneath the courtyard well, revealing where the rest of the 1943 famine hoard is buried. With the help of sweeper Manju, who holds a dark secret about the past sacrifices, Subimal tries to break the seal before the ghost drags him into the lime pit forever.

14.fmt: two friends telling ghost stories at night, and one story becomes real
14.title: ছায়াচিত্রের অভিশাপ 📜
14.summary: On an ominous, stormy Kartik afternoon in Baranagar, paper restorer Anirban Sen is visited by his estranged schoolmate Suman Majumdar, who arrives soaked in river silt and carrying an antique silver-clasped photo album. Anirban feels guilty for ignoring Suman's desperate phone calls three nights ago. As the power fails and gale winds lash the mansion, Suman insists they review the vintage prints. With each turned plate from 1918 to 1923, an emaciated specter with tetanic clawed hands creeps closer to the lens. Anirban discovers the photographs were taken inside this very house, once the quarantine death-den of Pramatha Roy, who died of locked-jaw tetanus. Horrifyingly, Suman's skin is freezing, his pupils are fixed, and Plate 5 suddenly shows this current room in real-time, revealing a waterlogged corpse lurking beneath Anirban's desk while Suman blocks the only exit.
14.part2_plan: Part 2 begins at the immediate cliffhanger: Anirban must deal with the trapped manifestation under his desk while confronting the fact that Suman drowned three days ago at Nimtala Ghat. Depending on the viewer vote, Anirban either tries to forcefully drag Suman's waterlogged shell out toward the flooded courtyard, or confronts the spirit of Pramatha Roy using paper restoration solvents and consecrated lamp oil to break the album's psychic seal. Anirban must race to extinguish the ritual Akash Prodip on the rain-swept terrace before the sixth and final plate develops fully, threatening to transfer Pramatha's soul into Anirban's living flesh.

plot_holes_fixed: Fixed the abrupt jump in previous draft where the glass negative appeared spontaneously in Anirban's kurta pocket: added precise setup in dialogue and narration explaining that Suman slipped the negative when grabbing Anirban's shoulder during their standoff.

Clarified why Anirban had windproof lighter and volatile solvents readily available: established his profession as an archivist and paper conservator working with restoration spirits (acetone, denatured alcohol, dissolved camphor) on his workbench.

Resolved the logical contradiction of the ghost burning: the entity Pramatha Roy was bound to the silver-halide photo emulsions and the ancestral property; burning the plate severed his tie to Suman's corpse while fulfilling the trap of forcing Anirban to mirror the final exposure.
Addressed why Suman's body didn't decay immediately: preserved by cold saline Hooghly river silt and held upright by the rigor mortis of the tetanus curse until the final ritual release.
Ensured character names and relationships are stated explicitly in the live audio dialogue and narrator bridges across every scene for immediate audio-drama clarity.

plot_outline: Anirban kicks his chair backward as bloated grey hands clutch the desk frame from below.
Suman speaks with a choked, hollow cadence, confirming he drowned seventy-two hours ago at Nimtala Ghat.
Anirban refuses to inspect the final plate and grabs his restoration tray of pure alcohol and acetone.
Pramatha Roy's spirit begins emerging from the knee-hole of the desk, filling the room with the stench of river silt.
Suman reveals that the terrace Akash Prodip lantern is anchoring the dead zamindar's crossing into living flesh.
Anirban dashes restorative solvent directly into Suman's possessed face, forcing the rigid corpse to stumble aside.
Anirban unlatches the study door and flees into the pitch-black, storm-battered corridor toward the roof stairs.
Lightning reveals wet, barefoot footprints ascending the staircase ahead of Anirban.
Reaching the rain-swept terrace, Anirban spots the wicker Akash Prodip burning against impossible cyclone winds.
Pramatha Roy manifests directly on the terrace balustrade, blocking the lantern with tetanic, clawed arms.
Anirban attempts to snuff out the flame with rain, but the wick feeds on spirit energy and river oil.
Suman's dripping shell arrives on the terrace, cornering Anirban against the fragile brick parapet.
Suman's throat emits a moment of his genuine living voice, begging Anirban to destroy the album's silver master negative.
Anirban pulls the silver-clasped fifth plate negative from his kurta pocket, realizing it was planted on him.
Using his brass restoration lighter and remaining chemical solvent, Anirban sets the antique glass plate on fire.
Pramatha Roy lets out a bone-chilling shriek as the photographic silver emulsion bubbles and disintegrates.
With the negative destroyed, the Akash Prodip shatters in a blue flash, banishing the aristocrat's shadow into the tempest.
Suman's lifeless body collapses onto the wet terrace tiles, finally free of the parasitic spirit.
At dawn, the police and river patrol retrieve Suman's body, verifying he died three days earlier in the river.
Back in his study, Anirban looks into his pocket mirror and finds his jaw muscles spasming into an unnatural lock.
